RC TIME CONSTANTS OPERATION
OBJECTIVES
w Observe capacitor charging and discharging using a multimeter.
w Observe capacitor charging and discharging using an oscilloscope.
w Verify RC time constants by the use of measurements............................
. The experiment in this lesson is not setup to use the selected trainer.
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
Nida Experiment Card PC130 - 15
Capacitors take time to charge or discharge. The RC time constant equals the resistance times the capacitance.
INTRODUCTIONM
Using a multimeter or oscilloscope, the charge and discharge cycle of a capacitor can be monitored.

LESSON MENU
This experiment demonstrates RC Time Constants. You will apply a DC voltage to a series RC circuit and observe the charging and discharging of the capacitor using a multimeter and oscilloscope.
EXPERIMENT
Pick up the PC130-15 card. The purpose of this card is to demonstrate RC time constants.
1. Set the Test Console Controls to their initial control settings........
2. Set the Voltmeter Switch to Positive.
3. Set the Positive Supply Voltage to 10. The Test Console's voltage Meter should indicate 10 volts. SCAN FCC 0 External program = SCAN PWR 0 111
4. Carefully place the PC130-15 into the Test Console PC1 position. SCAN FTR 0 C1 00
EXPERIMENT CARD PLACEMENT - PC130-15 shown in PC1 position.

5. Set PC130-15 switches S1 through S5 to DOWN. ION DO NOT set PC130-15 S5 UP when PC1 DC Power is applied. S5 is used to discharge the capacitors and will short the + DC power supply to ground unless PC DC Power is OFF.
DO NOT set PC130-15 S5 UP when PC1 DC Power is applied. S5 is used to discharge the capacitors and will short the + DC power supply to ground unless PC DC Power is OFF.

The experiment is now set up. Let's use a multimeter to observe the charging and discharging of a capacitor.
1. Connect your multimeter across capacitor C3.
2. Set the multimeter range to 10 volts.
LEAD PLACEMENT - To measure C3, place test leads across TP1 and TP4.

3. While observing the meter, place S3 to UP on PC130-15. Notice how long it took for C3 to charge to 10 volts. The RC time constant equals 2.2 seconds. It takes 11 seconds for C3 to fully charge. isconnect the multimeter.
LEAD PLACEMENT - S3 Up (Closed), Place test leads across TP1 and TP4.
CALCULATING RC TIME CONSTANT - It takes 5 TCs to fully charge a capacitor. One time constant for C3 is 2.2 seconds, so it takes 11 seconds for C3 to charge.
Now, let's observe the discharging of a capacitor.
4. Disconnect the meter and set the PC1 DC switch to OFF. The multimeter must be disconnected. If not, the capacitor will discharge through the meter.
The multimeter must be disconnected. If not, the capacitor will discharge through the meter.k
